nodes.name: Policy draft needs controls, not contradiction handling
nodes.description: Mike's data-classification policy draft does not supersede the brain's existing financial-isolation doctrine. It is a gap to fix: the draft needs enforceable language for ownership, exceptions, unlabeled data, Purview label mapping, and NAC vs Interplastic financial isolation before it can safely govern Fabric assets.

nodes.name: ELT steward decision path is the gate
nodes.description: The next ELT-oriented conversation should be treated as a governance decision-rights checkpoint, not as another Fabric explanation. Evidence from the 2026-05-06 stand-up and Mike's modernization framing points to the same dependency: named data stewards are needed before domain assignments and phase 2 pilots can move.

nodes.name: Citrine needs a governed read path, not another spreadsheet workaround
nodes.description: The May 19 Citrine session shows cook-parameter analysis is still not moving: data exists or was extracted, but Mark still needs Robert/Ryan time, and programmatic ingestion is blocked by on-prem SQL access. The near-term PCD review should define a governed read path.

nodes.name: ADR-0004 turns Purview governance into a license-gated enforcement stack
nodes.description: The governance conversation has moved past policy wording. ADR-0004 names the actual enforcement layers, but several depend on licensing or ownership that is not confirmed. The next risk is designing against tools IP Corp may not own or has not operationalized.

nodes.name: Gold domain selection needs one fast proof and one strategic track
nodes.description: The promoted May 20 Fabric Weekly Stand-Up confirms the earlier live signal: domain selection, steward assignment, and Gold-model rollout are coupled. The next meeting should separate a quick-value proof domain from longer-tail strategic domain work so the program can show progress without pretending large domains are simple.

nodes.name: Sales BI clone drift is the strongest proof for governed Gold models
nodes.description: The Power BI sweep turned the Gold-domain argument into evidence: Interplastic, MP, and NAC Sales BI models share a template, but same-name measures have drifted. This is exactly the failure mode a governed domain semantic model is supposed to prevent.

nodes.name: The plant floor exposed non-system records as the real governance gap
nodes.description: The May 19 plant tour reframes the MDM/Fabric problem: the most important production and R&D records are not always in MES/M3/Optiva. Paper charge sheets, pilot reactor batch numbers, thumb-drive submittal packages, and lab notebooks are now first-class governance risks.

nodes.name: Source identity must be settled before pipeline simplification
nodes.description: Three separate May 19-20 signals point to the same risk: IP Corp can simplify Fabric ingestion, but only after naming the real source-of-truth and hidden staging transformations. M3 Cloud, ETQ, Salesforce/M3 staging, and direct SQL mirroring are converging into one source-binding decision.

nodes.name: The steward workshop is now the operating-model bridge
nodes.description: The May 20 Fabric Weekly Stand-Up turns the post-ELT steward problem from an abstract governance ask into a concrete workshop design problem: narrow the SharePoint list, wait for Mike feedback, define domains, and leave a working session with candidate names. That is the bridge between ELT alignment and business-owned domains.

nodes.name: Gold semantic models are becoming the control surface
nodes.description: The May 20 Power BI source-mapping discussion and existing enforcement ADR now converge on a stronger pattern: domain Gold semantic models should be treated as the governed reporting contract and access-control surface, not just another presentation layer artifact.

nodes.name: Intercompany modeling should preserve shared master data
nodes.description: The May 20 intercompany item discussion strengthens the master-data stance: avoid duplicating item numbers across companies when M3 can preserve one item definition and express company-specific behavior through maintained relationships, masks, and intercompany transaction flow.

nodes.name: Patrick's 1:1 is the pre-OOO decision gate
nodes.description: The May 26 Patrick 1:1 is now the highest-leverage near-term meeting because it sits between the post-ELT recalibration, Mike feedback dependency, steward workshop planning, and Patrick's 2026-05-28 through 2026-06-03 OOO window.

nodes.name: Plant-floor truth now has a canonical evidence map
nodes.description: The May 19 plant-tour findings moved from meeting evidence into a dedicated plant-floor source-of-record map, updated MES caveats, data-flow extensions, stakeholder notes, glossary terms, and risks R-020/R-021. Natively should use the May 27 follow-up packet as a source-of-record validation checklist, not a generic tour prompt.

nodes.name: Stakeholder brain frontend now has a visual direction
nodes.description: Steve added a concrete product-design preference for the stakeholder-facing brain frontend: keep Stitch creative freedom, but borrow Unabyss-style dark layered surfaces, crisp source/status chips, and motion that makes scattered context feel gathered into an intelligence layer. That should shape the sanitized access path without changing the Natively live runtime boundary.

nodes.name: Calendar actions need executable event coordinates, not just intent
nodes.description: The Fabric cadence reset was directionally right, but the outcome ledger shows five failed execution attempts because the calendar proposal lacked subject, start, and end. Natively should keep this as a follow-up until exact current and target event fields are confirmed.

nodes.name: Context capsule exposed a live 1:1 that the packet index had missed
nodes.description: A local Natively context capsule generated a high-confidence prep surface for the 2026-05-27 Steve/Patrick 1:1, while the durable Natively meeting index still pointed at the older 2026-05-26 packet and treated that lane as missing a post-meeting capture. The fix is to promote useful capsules into compact prep packets during the brain refresh, without promoting them into canonical meeting memory.

nodes.name: Plant-floor traceability now has a proposed evidence-stream contract
nodes.description: ADR-0006 proposes that Traceability Gold must not certify a combined plant-floor view until MES, paper charge sheets, PLC transfer logs, lab notebooks, CIPP packages, Optiva, Salesforce LSRs, QC/ANV/OATES, retains/rework, and NIR readings each have explicit owner, storage, authority, digital coverage, and lineage fields.

nodes.name: Disabled proactive coaching still emitted a live suggestion
nodes.description: A short May 27 Natively capture shows the assistant emitted a SAY THIS coaching line during a manual session immediately before Steve said he had disabled proactive meeting coaching mode. Treat this as a Natively live-mode gate risk, not IP Corp architecture evidence.

nodes.name: Pryor SSRS reporting is the first concrete test of the OT-to-Azure boundary
nodes.description: The newly recovered Pryor W34293 capture ties three threads together: Purdue-model enforcement, Azure-bound edge data collection, and Will's existing corporate SSRS reports. The non-obvious risk is not only where the Optix/Azure relay lives; it is whether reporting moves data up, moves reports down into OT, or creates a one-off exception that weakens the security pattern.

nodes.name: Knowledge-base access is now a stakeholder deliverable, not just an internal tool
nodes.description: Patrick asked for a link to the IP Corp knowledge-base layer after Steve described a searchable interface over meetings, decisions, source discussions, and Power BI/report-model analyses. That creates a useful stakeholder-alignment path, but it also turns repo exposure into an access-control and redaction problem.

nodes.name: Fabric cadence should pause once, then return as a synthesis session
nodes.description: The May 27 live capture indicates this week's Fabric stand-up should be canceled because there is not enough new material yet, while next week's Fabric discussion should be extended or moved after Steve organizes onsite transcripts and domain takeaways.

nodes.name: Meeting visual briefs need a packet contract
nodes.description: The strongest new product hook is not just a prettier stakeholder frontend; it is a per-meeting visual brief artifact generated from the same processed meeting context and shown as the meeting or packet hero. Natively already has skipped meeting-infographic status records, so the next useful step is to define the sanitized artifact contract before changing app code.

nodes.name: Stakeholder access now needs a formal read-model boundary
nodes.description: The May 27 Patrick touchpoint, the repo's internal-only rules, and the Natively runtime contract now converge on one decision: Patrick/Eudias should see a curated read-only surface, not the raw architecture-brain repo. ADR-0007 captures that boundary as proposed architecture.

nodes.name: Old governance email request needs confirmation
nodes.description: A newly exported Natively backfill surfaced an April 13 request from Steve to draft an email to Robin, Patrick, and Mike with the IP Corp Data Governance PDF attached. The request is concrete but stale and outbound-stakeholder-facing, so the useful action is a confirmation follow-up before any draft is created.

nodes.name: DHS background capture stays indexed-only
nodes.description: The May 31 Natively auto-export captured a short DHS funding reconciliation/background broadcast segment plus Steve testing whether Natively could hear him and see the screen. It has no IP Corp architecture decisions, commitments, stakeholders, or calendar match, so it should remain indexed-only and should not feed prep packets or canonical project memory.

nodes.name: Generated infographic reports need a quality gate
nodes.description: Three new Natively meeting-infographic artifacts were generated after the prior refresh. One Pryor OT/Azure run failed during suggested-report retrieval, while two completed suggestion files returned generic or off-topic report templates instead of IP Corp meeting-specific follow-up ideas. These artifacts should stay out of live readiness context until the report-suggestion lane has a meeting-specific quality gate.

nodes.name: Status reminder capsule over-matched Fabric prep context
nodes.description: A new Natively context capsule for a five-minute weekly status reminder pulled several Fabric/governance prep packets into live context even though the invite notes only describe the weekly project status deck process. The brain should publish a reminder-specific packet and keep the deeper Fabric material as background until the invite or a live capture proves those topics are actually in scope.

nodes.name: Purview advisory split the work into catalog governance and DLP enforcement
nodes.description: The June 3 CDW/Purview session clarified that Steve's immediate data-team need is MDM classification, cataloging, lineage, and Fabric metadata governance, while CDW initially framed Purview around information protection, sensitivity labels, and DLP. The useful next move is a scoped follow-up that separates the catalog/MDM track, the DLP/enforcement track, and the license/admin boundary between them.
